hero.lead: A nation of 34.6 million with minerals that earn an eighth of the economy and forest across half its land, where the World Bank finances wastewater, fiscal resilience and tourism.

capital.heading: Mineral wealth, and safe water for every home.

register.name: Sustainable global bonds, 12 and 30 years
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · announced 10 November 2026 · coupons of 6.06% (12 years) and 6.45% (30 years) · spreads of 42 and 40 basis points · under the Sustainable Bond Framework of Peru, approved May 2026
register.note: Demand above US$21 billion from more than 320 accounts; the largest dollar bond issue in Peru’s history
register.text: Sustainable global bonds of the Republic of Peru, sold in dollars under the Sustainable Bond Framework approved in May 2026, whose proceeds are to finance programmes and projects to reduce social gaps. The categories named for this issue are climate change adaptation, disaster risk management and resilient infrastructure; no one of the seven standards is named. An exchange offer was launched for dollar bonds due 2027, 2030 and 2031, in return for new bonds due 2038.

register.name: Sustainable and social global bonds of 2021
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · outstanding in June 2026 · sustainable bonds of US$2.25bn due 2034 at 3.000% and US$1bn due 2072 at 3.600%, issued 2 November 2021 · social bond of €1bn due 2036 at 1.950%, issued 17 November 2021
register.note: Three of the 20 global bonds outstanding in June 2026 carry a sustainable or social label
register.text: Sustainable and social bonds of the Republic of Peru, issued in the international market in November 2021 and still outstanding in June 2026. The Ministry’s table gives their label and terms, not the spending they financed.

register.name: Arequipa–Colca tourism corridor
register.detail: World Bank · IBRD loan · approved 9 July 2026 · total cost $97.8M, including $20.6M in counterpart funding · executed by the Regional Government of Arequipa
register.note: About 173,000 people live near the infrastructure and sites to be improved
register.text: A World Bank loan for strategic investments in the Arequipa region across tourism, culture, transport, water and sanitation, health, environmental conservation and destination management. Its water, sanitation and health investments serve the water, shelter and health standards for the communities along the corridor.

register.name: Wastewater management and circular economy
register.detail: World Bank · IBRD · approved 30 September 2025 · multi-phase 10-year programme · Lima and Puno
register.note: In Puno the programme focuses on protecting Lake Titicaca
register.text: A World Bank programme to upgrade water and sanitation systems in Lima and Puno, improving infrastructure and expanding access to clean water, with wastewater management, water reuse and aquifer recharge. It serves the water standard, the furthest from reach in Peru.

register.name: Economic resilience and climate adaptation
register.detail: World Bank · IBRD · approved 26 March 2025 · press release of 27 March 2025
register.note: Adds water supply and sanitation as an adaptation sector
register.text: A World Bank programme to boost Peru’s economic resilience and climate adaptation, covering water supply and sanitation, renewables, distributed generation and electromobility, disaster risk management and territorial planning. It serves the water and energy standards.

register.name: Residential solar power in the Peruvian Amazon, Acciona.org Perú
register.detail: IDB Invest · project 15243-01 · approval date 29 October 2025 · senior A loan · with a $3.5M blended finance senior loan from vehicles managed by IDB Invest
register.note: Third-generation home solar systems for new isolated communities, and new solar microgrids with battery storage and smart metering
register.text: An IDB Invest loan to Acciona.org Perú, which provides energy solutions to isolated rural communities, to install home solar systems in new communities, replace older systems and build solar microgrids. It serves the energy standard for homes beyond the grid.

register.name: Water, sanitation and storm drainage for Juliaca
register.detail: IDB · conditional credit line of $700M approved 13 December 2023 (PE-O0010) · first individual loan (PE-L1285) · 15-year repayment, 7-year grace · $75M local contribution · in implementation
register.note: To benefit 300,000 people, about 100,000 households, with new or improved drinking water and sewerage connections
register.text: An IDB loan to Peru for drinking water supply and sewerage works in Juliaca, in the Puno region, and to strengthen the water company SEDAJuliaca. It serves the water standard directly; approved in December 2023, it is listed as an older instrument still active.

register.name: Drinking water and sanitation for Zarumilla and Aguas Verdes
register.detail: IDB · PE-L1256, loan 5737/OC-PE · approved 11 January 2023 · 15-year repayment, 7-year grace · total nearly $78M with the local contribution · executed by Agua Tumbes · in implementation
register.note: 7,050 homes to connect to drinking water for the first time; about 11,900 families to receive wastewater services
register.text: An IDB loan for new wells, reservoirs, pumping stations, household connections and treatment plants in the Zarumilla and Aguas Verdes districts of Tumbes. It will improve the lives of nearly 50,000 people and serves the water standard; approved in January 2023, it is listed as an older instrument still active.

register.name: Comprehensive Rural Water and Sanitation Program, Phase II (PIASAR II)
register.detail: IDB · PE-L1269, loan 5628/OC-PE · approved 26 October 2022 · total programme cost $232.2M, with $82.2M in local contributions · 15-year repayment, 7-year grace · Ministry of Housing, Construction and Sanitation, through the National Rural Sanitation Program · in implementation
register.note: The works will connect rural homes, healthcare centres, schools and social organisations to water and sanitation
register.text: An IDB loan to bring drinking water and sanitation services to rural populations in Peru. It serves the water standard where coverage is lowest; approved in October 2022, it is listed as an older instrument still active.

register.name: Credit for women-led micro and small enterprises, Caja Arequipa
register.detail: JICA · loan agreement signed 5 December 2025 · borrower Caja Municipal de Ahorro y Crédito de Arequipa
register.note: All of JICA’s funds go to lending to women-led small and micro enterprises; JICA also supports training for women entrepreneurs
register.text: A JICA loan to Caja Arequipa, Peru’s largest municipal credit and savings bank, to expand credit for micro and small enterprises led by women. It serves the livelihood standard, contributing to more employment for women and smaller income disparities.

register.name: Financial inclusion of micro and small enterprises in the north, Mibanco
register.detail: JICA · Private Sector Investment Finance · signed 6 May 2025 in Lima · co-financed with IDB Invest under CORE
register.note: 70% to be sub-lent in eight northern regions and 30% to micro and small businesses run by women across the country
register.text: A JICA loan to Mibanco, a Peruvian microfinance bank, to improve access to finance for micro and small enterprises, especially in the northern regions. It serves the livelihood standard and is meant to reduce regional disparities.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Metals and minerals already earn; the task is to keep more of their value at home.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 23.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Waposat
items.text: A company from Huancavelica that installs real-time water quality monitoring and control systems, with 26 stations in small cities and more in rural areas, to close the gap for rural people without safe water, reaching more than 100,000 people in 15 regions.

items.name: Acciona.org Perú
items.text: A private social initiative that brings electricity from home solar systems and solar microgrids to isolated rural communities, with IDB Invest financing approved in October 2025, and granted a rural electricity concession in October 2025 to supply 1,490 homes in 48 localities of Cajamarca, Cusco and Loreto.

items.name: Laboratoria
items.text: A non-profit that trains women to start careers in technology through bootcamps, mainly in programming, and sells corporate membership plans through which companies such as Interbank, Yape and Ripley invest in training their women staff, with operations in Peru and nine other countries.

items.name: VIDAWASI
items.text: An organisation that brings specialised children’s health care beyond Lima from its Ciudadela de Salud Infantil in Urubamba, Cusco, with more than 120,000 child and family health services reported, and whose Plaza Yanahuara convention centre earns income to help finance its medical and social work.

items.name: Umayux Technology
items.text: A Peruvian company from Cusco that develops and manufactures phototherapy equipment for neonatal jaundice, with which more than 5,000 newborns have been treated in public hospitals.

items.name: Financiera ProEmpresa
items.text: A microfinance institution, financed by Oikocredit since 2006, that offers loans, microinsurance and savings to micro-entrepreneurs in several regions of Peru, with 55,481 active borrowers, 49.7% of them women and 34.5% rural.

items.name: Alternativa
items.text: A centre for social research and popular education in northern Lima whose microfinance programme, started in 1994 to support women entrepreneurs, lends through village banks of around 15 members, with 2,964 clients, 86% of them women.

items.name: Cooperativa Agraria Cafetalera ACPC Pichanaki
items.text: A cooperative of around 270 small coffee farmers in Junín that sells their coffee on the international specialty market without intermediaries, gives technical assistance and runs social projects on food security and women’s empowerment.
